extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners advising on double patenting issues)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners) on identifying, analyzing, and handling statutory and nonstatutory double patenting issues (including provisional rejections, terminal disclaimer practice, patent term filing date determinations, and reexamination/reissue considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances where double patenting issue can be raised
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting issue may arise between two or more pending applications, or between one or more pending applications and a patent. A double patenting issue may likewise arise in a reexamination proceeding between the patent claims being reexamined and the claims of one or more applications and/or patents. Double patenting does not relate to international applications which have not yet entered the national stage in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting may be implicated where there is a shared inventive entity, at least one common joint inventor, a common applicant, and/or a common owner/assignee, or where inventions result from activities within the scope of a joint research agreement as defined in 35 U.S.C. 102(c) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2) and (3). Examiner must evaluate facts of record to determine whether second grant would give an unjustified extension of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between an issued patent and one or more applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting may exist between an issued patent and an application which share the same inventive entity, at least one common (joint) inventor, a common applicant, and/or a common owner/assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a first patent has issued, the examiner must determine whether granting a second patent would unjustly extend rights granted in the first patent (e.g., consider ownership, inventive entity, joint research agreements). Case law (e.g., In re Hubbell) shows complete identity of ownership/inventive entities is not always required. Use statutory or nonstatutory basis as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between copending applications — when provisional rejections are permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may become aware of two or more copending applications that share common inventive entity/applicant/owner or claim inventions resulting from joint research agreement activity, that would raise double patenting if one became a patent. Courts have sanctioned making applicant aware via a provisional rejection when confidential status can be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published (unredacted) applications can be used as double patenting references without violating confidentiality; unpublished or redacted-published applications may be used only if at least one common inventor/applicant/assignee exists or they are deemed commonly owned. Provisional rejections may be made and maintained until obviated or no longer applicable. See MPEP §§ 2136.01 and 2154.01(d) for provisional rejection background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting (NSDP) rejection — required responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete response to a nonstatutory double patenting (NSDP) rejection is either a reply by applicant showing that the claims subject to the rejection are patentably distinct from the reference claims, or the filing of a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321 in the pending application(s) with a reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a response is required even when the NSDP rejection is provisional. Filing a terminal disclaimer or showing patentable distinctness is necessary for further consideration of the rejection, and the filing should not be held in abeyance. An application must not be allowed unless compliant terminal disclaimer(s) are filed and/or the withdrawal of the NSDP rejection(s) is made of record by the examiner. See MPEP § 1490 for terminal disclaimer discussion and MPEP § 714.03 for replies with omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer practice for multiple copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more pending applications each contain provisional NSDP rejections over the others, provisional NSDP rejections will be made in each application. Where three applications conflict and terminal disclaimers are necessary, it is not sufficient to file a terminal disclaimer in only one application addressing the other two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appropriate terminal disclaimer must be filed in at least two of the applications to require common ownership/enforcement for all three applications. In certain situations a terminal disclaimer may be required in each application. See MPEP § 1490, subsection VI.D for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term filing date for original utility or plant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent term filing date of an original utility or plant application filed on or after June 8, 1995 is the earliest of: (1) the actual filing date of the application; or (2) the filing date of the earliest application for which the application claims the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d)/(f), 365(a)/(b), or 386(a)/(b) are NOT taken into account when determining patent term filing date. Determination of entitlement to the earlier filing's disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) is not required when calculating patent term filing date. Consult 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP § 211 for proper benefit claim practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when provisional NSDP is the only rejection remaining (earlier/same/later patent term filing date rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional NSDP rejection is the only rejection remaining in an application, treatment depends on relative patent term filing dates between the application under examination and the reference application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application under examination has the earlier patent term filing date, withdraw the rejection and permit that application to issue (converting the provisional rejection in the other application into NSDP upon issuance). If both have the same patent term filing date, maintain the provisional NSDP until overcome (applicant may show patentable distinctness or file compliant terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321). If the application under examination has the later patent term filing date, maintain the rejection until applicant overcomes it. If PTAB decision did not reach provisional NSDP and reference has issued, re-issue as nonprovisional rejection and require terminal disclaimer; if reference abandoned or never matured and provisional DP is the only remaining rejection, withdraw it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design applications and pre-URAA (pre-June 8, 1995) utility/plant application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent term is measured from the issue date (so patent term filing date determination not necessary for designs). For utility/plant applications filed prior to June 8, 1995 consult supervisory personnel to determine whether provisional NSDP rejections should be withdrawn or not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provisional double patenting rejection is the only rejection remaining in the earlier-filed design application, withdraw that rejection and permit issue. For cross-type analyses (design vs utility/plant), consult TQAS or SPE for appropriate action. See subsection guidance in MPEP § 804.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional statutory double patenting rejections (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims of an application are the same as those of a first patent they are barred under 35 U.S.C. 101 — the statutory basis for a double patenting rejection. A rejection based on double patenting of the 'same invention' finds support in 35 U.S.C. 101; 'same invention' means identical subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory (35 U.S.C. 101) double patenting rejection can be overcome only by canceling or amending the conflicting claims so they are no longer coextensive in scope; filing a terminal disclaimer cannot overcome a statutory double patenting rejection. Use form paragraphs 8.30 (heading) and 8.31 (rejection against an issued patent) or 8.32 (provisional rejection against copending application) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between one or more applications and a published application — provisional rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A published patent application and an application may give rise to double patenting where they share inventive entity/common applicant/common owner, or result from joint research agreement activities. If the published application has not yet issued as a patent, the examiner may make a provisional rejection on the ground of double patenting when the published application has not been abandoned and its pending claims conflict with the application being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional handling parallels other provisional double patenting guidance; statutory double patenting cannot be obviated by terminal disclaimer. See subsection B and other provisional rejection guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between a patent and a reissue application or patent under reexamination — URAA / post-URAA vs pre-URAA rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a potential NSDP arises between related patents (in reissue or reexamination), determine whether the patents are subject to the same patent term statutory law (post-URAA vs pre-URAA) because expiration-date rules affect obviousness-type double patenting analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-URAA earlier-expiring patents can be obviousness-type nonstatutory double patenting references for later-expiring patents (Gilead/Gilead line); when one patent is pre-URAA the earlier issuance date interplay may alter availability as a reference (see Novartis v. Breckenridge). Consult TC Quality Assurance Specialist if factual application of these precedents is unclear. See MPEP § 804.05 for patent term extension impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceedings can address double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting issue may raise a substantial new question of patentability of a claim and thus can be addressed in a reexamination proceeding. Double patenting may exist where the reference patent/application and the patent under reexamination share inventive entity/common applicant/owner, and (for patents granted on or after Dec 10, 2004) may arise from joint research agreement activity if evidence is made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art exceptions like 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or disqualification under pre-AIA 103(c) generally cannot be used to overcome a double patenting rejection or NSDP, and an excepted reference cannot be used as a secondary reference in a NSDP obviousness-type rejection. See MPEP §§ 717.02, 2154.02(c), 2146, and 2258 for reexamination-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of a double patenting rejection (statutory vs nonstatutory and 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a double patenting rejection is appropriate, it must be based on statutory grounds or nonstatutory grounds. The ground employed depends upon the relationship of the inventions being claimed. A double patenting rejection is generally not permitted where the claimed subject matter is presented in a divisional application as a result of a restriction requirement made in a parent application under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must determine: (A) whether a statutory basis exists; (B) whether a nonstatutory basis exists; and (C) whether a nonstatutory DP rejection is prohibited by the third sentence of 35 U.S.C. 121. Make these determinations on the basis of all facts in the application. Charts in MPEP § 804 illustrate the methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domination vs double patenting — distinction and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Domination and double patenting are separate issues. One patent/application 'dominates' a second when the first has a broad claim that fully encompasses an invention defined in a narrower claim in another patent/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domination by itself, absent statutory or nonstatutory double patenting grounds, cannot support a double patenting rejection (In re Kaplan; In re Sarett). However, domination does not preclude a double patenting rejection — it may be present alongside proper statutory/nonstatutory grounds (see In re Schneller, AbbVie v. Kennedy Institute). Evaluate domination as a factual circumstance but rely on statutory/nonstatutory legal bases for rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory double patenting test — 'same invention' (35 U.S.C. 101) and literal-infringement test
rubrics_metrics.description: A reliable test for double patenting under 35 U.S.C. 101 is whether a claim in the application could be literally infringed without literally infringing a corresponding claim in the patent. 'Same invention' means identical subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there exists an embodiment that falls within the scope of one claim but not the other, identical subject matter is not present and statutory double patenting does not exist. Examples: a claim reciting 'halogen' is broader than a claim reciting 'chlorine' (not identical); a claim reciting '36 inches' and one reciting '3 feet' define the same invention. If determined the same invention is being claimed twice, 35 U.S.C. 101 precludes the second patent regardless of terminal disclaimers. Use form paragraphs 8.30–8.32 as applicable; follow examiner notes regarding when to use each form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and examiner practice for double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use designated form paragraphs for double patenting rejections: ¶ 8.30 (heading for statutory type), ¶ 8.31 (Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 101, Double Patenting — against an issued patent), and ¶ 8.32 (Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 101, Double Patenting — against copending application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 8.30 must be used as a heading for subsequent statutory (same invention) double patenting rejections. ¶ 8.31 is used only for double patenting over an earlier patent (not copending applications); ¶ 8.32 is used only for double patenting over a copending application. Examiner notes enumerate additional required paragraphs (e.g., 7.15.fti, 7.19.fti) and conditions (pre-AIA/FITF handling, additional form paragraphs like 8.27.aia, 8.28.fti/aia) and include instructions on bracket insertions and when to make provisional rejections in the reference application.
